title: Antibiotic Disk Testing
author: Aubrey Reed
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ugfettn

steps.title: Prepare overnight culture
steps.instruction: Fill a sterile 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube with 1 mL of the appropriate liquid medium (LB if the colony is from an LB agar plate, or TSA if from a TSA plate). Using a sterile loop, pick a single colony from the corresponding agar plate and suspend it in the media tube. Incubate the tube at the appropriate temperature (typically 37 °C) for overnight growth, or for 2–3 days if longer incubation is required.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of LB or TSA broth to a sterile Eppendorf tube
Inoculate with one colony using a sterile loop, matching agar and broth types
Incubate at the appropriate temperature for overnight (or 2–3 days)

steps.title: Plate culture and apply antibiotic
steps.instruction: Transfer 10 µL of the overnight culture onto a fresh agar plate, spread the inoculum evenly, place the antibiotic disk to be tested onto the plate as illustrated, incubate the plate for 24 hours, then measure the diameter of the inhibition zone and compare it to reference values to determine susceptibility.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 10 µL of the overnight culture onto the agar surface
Spread the inoculum uniformly with a sterile spreader
Place the antibiotic disk onto the plate as shown
Measure the inhibition‑zone diameter and compare with known standards
